text.p: Delgratia Mining Corp shares fell further on Friday after the company said it was too soon to specify the level of reserves on its Nevada gold project.
"I believe that it is premature to quantify the potential of this gold system," Charles Ager, president and chairman of Delgratia, said in a statement.

Delgratia said on Friday it had no knowledge of any material facts that would account for the recent fluctuations in the price of its stock. But Ager said he regretted media reports estimating the gold reserves at its 70 percent-owned Nevada project at five million ounces.

Delgratia stock was halted on Nasdaq today ahead of the release, then dropped 6 to 10 when trading resumed. The shares fell 17-5/8 to 16 on Thursday, after more than quadrupling since the start of 1997.
A Nevada mining official said late on Thursday that it was too soon for Delgratia to make claims about the size of the gold based on four drill holes.

"There's a long way to go before anyone can say with certainty that that's going to become a reality," Russ Fields, adminstrator for the Nevada Division of Minerals, told Reuters in a phone interview from Carson City.
Delgratia shares plunged on Thursday as questions arose over the project's value.

The company -- which is associated with Arakis Energy Corp former chief executive Terry Alexander -- released results from four widely-spaced drill holes on Wednesday and a company investor relations employee reportedly said they showed what could be a deposit of five million ounces of gold.

"These are widely spaced drill holes -- four drill holes -- it's not enough," Fields said. "Our world-class gold mines in the northern part of the state drill their properties on 200-foot centers. These holes are as far apart as 3,700 feet."
One analyst said even five million ounces would not justify the peaks the stock price reached in its run-up.
"My numbers at the time showed that you would need about 11 million ounces to justify where the stock was trading," said the analyst, who asked not to be identified.
